transcript: Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and Sundar Pichai just signed a promise nobody can enforce. Picture this: a fancy lunch at the White House. Around the table, Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, Sundar Pichai, Jensen Huang, and the bosses of OpenAI and Anthropic. Basically, the people building every AI on your phone. That same day, Trump signed an order: every American government office now has to stop writing AI and start writing SI, super intelligence. Here's the funny part: in tech, super intelligence means an AI smarter than every human at everything. Experts say we are not there yet. So America just named the baby before it was born. Then came the real deal: six AI companies signed a safety promise with four layers of checks. Their own team watches the AI, a second team watches that team, an outside auditor checks everything, and the company board gets the report card. Sounds strict, right? Here's the catch: if they break it, nothing happens. No law, no fine. Trump called it "morally binding," which is basically a pinky promise, a very, very expensive pinky promise. The next day, California Governor Gavin Newsom called it "reckless." Then he signed his own order. In California, AI stays AI. And the cherry on top, the official document about keeping AI safe spelled "United States" as "Unites States," right under Trump's signature. Jokes aside, this matters to us. Millions of Indians use ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Meta AI every day. If these companies check their own homework, our AI gets checked the same way. A new name, a new promise, and still no referee. Would you trust these companies to check themselves? Yes or no in the comments. I share updates like these in my WhatsApp community. Link in bio.
